=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible paired leaves attached at the same node on the stem)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely together at the terminal end of the shoot)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (individual leaves are undivided)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth edge without teeth)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): ovate (broadest near the base and tapering to the tip)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (wedge-shaped, narrowing towards the petiole)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible and evenly spaced, curving towards the leaf margin
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous and shiny (smooth surface with a noticeable sheen)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are visible but relatively short compared to the leaf blade)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (thin, flexible green stem typical of a young seedling)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent
    19.	Stem color: green (with some darker brownish tones at the nodes)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling shows clear signs of damage with multiple holes in the leaf margins and midribs. The leaves are arranged in a decussate pattern (opposite pairs at successive nodes). The leaf blades appear somewhat thick or leathery.
